six-days.title: Six Days and 13.8 Billion Years
six-days.hook: Science says 13.8 billion years. The Quran says “six days”. Here is the popular calculation that joins them, step by step, and where to be careful.
six-days.proofH: How the clocks and the ages were measured
six-days.science.0: The Quran says the heavens and the earth were created “in six days” (25:59, and six other verses). The Arabic word is yawm, a day, but the Quran also uses it for far longer spans: 22:47 says a day with your Lord is “like a thousand years of those which you count”, and 70:4 speaks of a day of fifty thousand years.
six-days.science.1: Science dates the universe to 13.8 billion years: ESA's Planck satellite measured 13.787 ± 0.020 billion years from the afterglow of the Big Bang. The Earth is younger, about 4.54 billion years old, from the radioactive dating of meteorites and the oldest rocks.
six-days.science.2: Time is not the same for everyone. Einstein's relativity says a clock runs slower when it moves fast or sits deeper in gravity, and this is measured every day: the clocks on GPS satellites would drift by about 38 microseconds a day if engineers did not correct them. Near a black hole the effect becomes enormous.
six-days.science.3: A popular reading takes each “day” as one sixth of cosmic history: 13.8 billion ÷ 6 ≈ 2.3 billion years. Verse 41:9 says the earth was created “in two days”, and two such days are 4.6 billion years, close to the Earth's measured age. Try the arithmetic in the lab below.

six-days.proof.0.title: Einstein: time is not the same for everyone
six-days.proof.0.text: Special relativity (1905) says a moving clock runs slow. General relativity (1915) adds that a clock deeper in gravity runs slow too. There is no single, universal clock.
six-days.proof.1.title: Patterson: the age of the Earth
six-days.proof.1.text: Clair Patterson measures lead isotopes in meteorites, including the Canyon Diablo iron, and finds that the Earth and the meteorites formed 4.55 ± 0.07 billion years ago.
six-days.proof.1.cap: A piece of the Canyon Diablo meteorite.
six-days.proof.2.title: Pound and Rebka: gravity slows clocks
six-days.proof.2.text: At Harvard's Jefferson Laboratory, gamma rays sent up and down a 22.5 m tower shift in frequency by the tiny amount general relativity predicts.
six-days.proof.2.cap: Jefferson Laboratory, Harvard, where the tower experiment was done.
six-days.proof.3.title: Hafele and Keating fly atomic clocks
six-days.proof.3.text: Four caesium atomic clocks are flown around the world on airliners, east and then west. Compared with clocks on the ground, they lose about 59 nanoseconds going east and gain about 273 going west, as relativity predicts.
six-days.proof.4.title: A clock lifted by 33 centimetres
six-days.proof.4.text: At NIST, two aluminium-ion clocks are so precise that raising one by 33 cm makes it measurably faster: time dilation at the height of a step.
six-days.proof.5.title: Planck: 13.8 billion years
six-days.proof.5.text: The final results of ESA's Planck satellite give the age of the universe as 13.787 ± 0.020 billion years, from its map of the cosmic microwave background.
six-days.fit.0: The Quran itself uses “day” for spans of a thousand and of fifty thousand years (22:47, 70:4), so reading the six days as long ages has a basis in the text.
six-days.fit.1: Relativity shows that the length of a “day” depends on whose clock measures it, something no one could test before the 20th century.
six-days.fit.2: On the equal-days reading, two days come to 4.6 billion years, about 1.3% from the Earth's measured age of 4.54 billion.
six-days.gap.0: The verses give no length for the days. Dividing by six assumes six equal days, and that step does not use time dilation at all.
six-days.gap.1: Two days × 2.3 billion is a length of time, not a date. It matches the Earth's age only if the earth's two days are the last two of the six.
six-days.gap.2: In 41:9–12 the earth is mentioned before the heaven, which was then still smoke. Early scholars already discussed the order of these days and how they add up to six; each reading moves the result.
six-days.gap.3: Time dilation is real and measured, but the Quran does not mention it, and there is no agreed clock by which to measure a divine “day”.
six-days.gap.4: This calculation is a modern reading that circulates online, not something the verses state.
